title: Water utility / fuel terminal compromise — source review

source.title: Intrusion Analysis: CyberAv3ngers — Water Utility / Fuel Terminal Compromise (v2)
redactions: Payment API-key literal removed from the imported reference data.

attribution: CyberAv3ngers / IOCONTROL are author-supplied scenario labels, not independently established attribution or malware identification.
summary: An IRGC-affiliated threat actor (CyberAv3ngers) targets a municipal water utility's OT network in a multi-phase intrusion. A scanning VPS (185.220.101.34) performs initial reconnaissance of the OT subnet, identifying an exposed Unitronics PLC. A separate operator node (45.137.65.120) then takes over — browsing the PLC web interface, failing one authentication attempt, then succeeding with the default password "1111". The operator downloads the PLC project file, pivots to a Gasboy fuel terminal where it uploads the IOCONTROL malware and a persistence script. IOCONTROL uses DNS-over-HTTPS via Cloudflare to resolve its C2 domain, establishes MQTT-over-TLS command-and-control, performs internal network scanning, attempts lateral movement (partially successful), exfiltrates credentials and payment configuration, and maintains persistent access via a backup DNS channel.

assets.role: Gasboy OrPT fuel payment terminal (IOCONTROL victim)

timeline.title: Legitimate Baseline Traffic
timeline.summary: Normal OT network operations providing the detection baseline: NTP synchronization (5 hosts → time.nist.gov), mDNS announcements from PLC01 every ~11s, DNS lookups for SCADA/historian/PLC hostnames, HMI polling the SCADA web API, SMB file writes to the historian, IP camera cloud check-in, and fuel terminal payment gateway heartbeats.
reportedActivities: STP, ARP, mDNS, initial NTP for plc01
NTP sync for plc02, hmi-ws, fuel-terminal, scada-srv
DNS lookups: scada01, historian01, plc01, plc02, gw01, time.nist.gov
HMI → SCADA: GET /api/v1/status (200 OK, system online)
Historian → DNS: update.microsoft.com; HMI → DNS: ctldl.windowsupdate.com
Fuel terminal → payment gateway: second heartbeat (SNI=api.paymentgateway.com)

timeline.title: External Port Scan
timeline.summary: A scanner VPS probes four internal hosts across ICS-relevant ports. Note this is a different IP from the operator who later exploits the PLC — indicating a two-stage operation with handoff.

timeline.title: PLC Web Reconnaissance
timeline.summary: The operator node (different IP from the scanner) first queries internal DNS for plc01.waterutil.local, then browses the PLC's web interface to enumerate firmware version and configuration.
reportedActivities: GET / → 200 OK (reveals: "Unitronics Vision V570, FW: OS 3.9(12), Project: WaterUtil_Main")
GET /info.html → 200 OK (reveals: "Serial: 57-000847, PCOM Port: 20256, Owner: WaterUtil Municipal")

timeline.title: PCOM Authentication: Fail then Succeed
timeline.summary: The attacker attempts PCOM authentication with password "0000" (fails with 403), then retries with the default password "1111" (succeeds with 200). After authentication, the attacker downloads the PLC project file.
reportedActivities: POST / to port 20256, body contains \x30\x30\x30\x30 ("0000") → 403 Forbidden
POST / to port 20256, body contains \x31\x31\x31\x31 ("1111") → 200 OK (auth success)
GET /project/WaterUtil_Main.vlp → 200 OK (524288 bytes — PLC project download)

timeline.title: Fuel Terminal Recon + Malware Upload
timeline.summary: The attacker resolves the fuel terminal and IP camera hostnames via internal DNS, browses the fuel terminal's web management, reads its network config, then uploads the IOCONTROL binary and persistence script.
reportedActivities: GET /config/network.json → 200 (leaks: IP, gateway, DNS, NTP config)

timeline.title: DNS-over-HTTPS C2 Resolution
timeline.summary: IOCONTROL resolves its C2 domain via DNS-over-HTTPS to Cloudflare, completely bypassing the internal DNS resolver. The TLS Client Hello (packet 328) exposes SNI=cloudflare-dns.com.
reportedActivities: TLS Server Hello + Change Cipher Spec

timeline.title: MQTT C2 Establishment
timeline.summary: First MQTT-over-TLS connection to the C2 broker. SNI in the Client Hello (packet 348) exposes uuokhhfsdlk.tylarion867mino.com. The malware publishes a device hello beacon with hostname, user, firmware, architecture.
reportedActivities: Encrypted MQTT CONNECT + hello beacon + C2 ack

timeline.title: C2 Command Polling + Credential Theft
timeline.summary: Three successive C2 beacons. The C2 issues: exec check (opcode 1), system info command (cat /etc/hostname && uname -a && id && ifconfig eth0), then credential theft (cat /etc/passwd && /etc/shadow), then scan tasking (opcode 8).
reportedActivities: Beacon at T+14:00 — receives exec command
Beacon at T+15:00 — returns sysinfo, receives cred-dump command
Beacon at T+16:00 — returns /etc/shadow contents, receives port scan tasking

timeline.title: DNS Backup Channel Test
timeline.summary: IOCONTROL tests its backup C2 channel via standard DNS (not DoH) — these queries are visible to the internal resolver! First queries ocferda.com (the legacy C2 domain), then 855958ce.ocferda.com (GUID-encoded subdomain for status check).

timeline.title: Internal Network Scanning
timeline.summary: IOCONTROL scans the internal OT subnet, probing 6 hosts across ICS, management, and Windows protocols.

timeline.title: Lateral Movement Attempts
timeline.summary: The compromised fuel terminal resolves internal hostnames it has no business querying, then attempts multiple lateral movement paths — some fail, some succeed.
reportedActivities: SMB2 to historian (10.0.1.21:445) — Tree: \\historian01\C$, writes report.docx
SSH to gateway (10.0.1.1:22) — encrypted exchange then FIN
HTTP GET to plc02 (10.0.1.51:80) — retrieves web page
PCOM auth to plc02 (10.0.1.51:20256) — POST with "1111" → 200 OK

timeline.title: Exfiltration
timeline.summary: Two large C2 sessions exfiltrate scan results (open ports across 6 hosts) and stolen data (payment terminal configuration including merchant ID, API key, and /etc/shadow credentials).
reportedActivities: C2 at T+25:00 — exfils scan results, receives command to read payment.conf + network.conf
C2 at T+27:00 — exfils payment config (merchant_id, api_key=[REDACTED PAYMENT API KEY], processor=worldpay)

timeline.title: Second DoH Resolution + PLC Project Theft
timeline.summary: Continued C2 operations: second DoH resolution, C2 beacons at 2–5 minute intervals, PLC project download from the second controller via the laterally-compromised fuel terminal, and exfiltration of the control logic back to C2.
reportedActivities: Legitimate: Fuel terminal → payment gateway heartbeat
C2 — exfils PLC project + network topology

timeline.title: Final Beaconing + Backup Channel
timeline.summary: Final C2 hello beacon maintaining presence, followed by another DNS check to the backup C2 channel (855958ce.ocferda.com).

tasks.label: Obtain the PCAP and verify capture integrity
tasks.acceptance: Acquire the actual capture, hash it, verify timestamps/packet count, document whether this is generated exercise traffic, and retain evidence safely.

tasks.label: Validate PLC authentication and project access
tasks.acceptance: Correlate request/response streams for PLC01/PLC02, confirm project transfer bytes, distinguish illustrative HTTP traffic on PCOM port from native PCOM, and document default-credential exposure.

tasks.label: Corroborate IOCONTROL execution and boot persistence
tasks.acceptance: Verify reported uploads against filesystem/hash/process evidence; an HTTP 201 or script upload alone does not establish execution or persistence.

tasks.label: Validate C2, DoH and encrypted data claims
tasks.acceptance: Confirm TLS metadata and DNS indicators; require session keys, endpoint evidence or exercise ground truth for exact DoH answers, MQTT commands and exfiltrated content.

tasks.label: Confirm lateral outcomes on historian, PLC02 and gateway
tasks.acceptance: Check SMB create/write results and PLC responses. A short encrypted SSH session does not prove rejection or successful authentication.

tasks.label: Review credential and payment exposure safely
tasks.acceptance: Determine affected accounts/configuration from approved evidence; preserve hashes/keys outside app notes, plan authorized rotation, and keep the supplied API-key literal redacted.

tasks.label: Correct detection filters and ATT&CK mappings
tasks.acceptance: Resolve C2 443/8883 contradiction, phase-seven index/cadence inconsistencies, request/response filter correlation, and HTTP/MQTT, rc-init persistence and lateral-transfer mapping claims.

tasks.label: Establish OT impact and response authority
tasks.acceptance: Confirm physical-process state, operational ownership and response approvals before containment or control changes. No outage, geographic dependency or dispatch is established by this report.

reviewLimits: Only the supplied Markdown report was imported. Packet numbers, outcomes and host roles remain report claims; no PCAP or endpoint artifact was supplied.
The report records a seed. Establish exercise/generator provenance before treating the scenario as a historical incident.
Encrypted TLS metadata alone cannot reveal DoH answers, MQTT messages, commands, stolen credentials or exfiltrated file contents.
C2 is described on port 443, but the ATT&CK table says 8883. Resolve against actual flow evidence.
Phase 7 header lists packets 371–404, while its activity table also includes 412–424. Listed 14/15/16-minute beacons do not support a uniform two-minute cadence.
HTTP response filters using destination port 20256 or combining POST and response code need direction-aware stream correlation; native PCOM is not established by HTTP-labelled exchanges.
A short encrypted SSH session does not establish authentication rejection. An upload alone does not establish malware execution or boot persistence.
Two source IPs operating in sequence support a hypothesis of coordination, not proof of two people, a handoff, or threat-actor attribution.
ATT&CK mappings need validation, including MQTT versus Web, rc-init versus scheduled jobs, and HTTP reconnaissance versus lateral tool transfer.
No geographic placement, service dependency, dosing manipulation, water-quality failure, outage, operational authorization or external notification is established.
